# order: EO:1992  (WPA 1944: 1914 July 15)
# WPA summary: Anna B. Frost made eligiblefor appointment as copyist in the Construction and Repair Bureau, Navy Dept.,without examination.1914 CSR 130. . [169 J
# book: Thirty-first Annual Report of the United States Civil Service Commission, fiscal year ended June 30, 1914
# scanned image 137, printed page 130; page lines 2-13
# source: https://archive.org/download/annualreport139commgoog/annualreport139commgoog_djvu.xml  sha256 748145327cc4747e27aefe00b5a3e31f5ebe8eb60b92a78e231aeb0237074ab1
# found by: monthday_and_names; date 1914-07-15; words anna|frost|repair
# Government printed copy (OCR of a compilation or report), not the signed original. A lead for the
# original_text step: read it against the scan before use. Exact slice of the page OCR follows.
----- EXACT SLICE -----
for services rendered to the Government in its military and naval branches. In view
of these facts the Secretary of War recommends the appointment of Mrs. Brown.
The Civil Service Comm i ssion does not concur in the recommendation of this order.
July 15, 1014.
Mrs. Anna B. Frost may be appointed to the position of copyist, at $900 per annum,
in the Bureau of Construction and Repair, Navy Department, without reference to
the requirement of examination under the civil-service rules.
Mrs. Frost is the wife of Mr. Floyd T. Frost, who has been continuously employed
in the Navy Department since March 8, 1890, and who has rendered faithful and
efficient service. In 1910 Mr. Frost suffered a stroke of paralysis, from which he has
never fully recovered, and at the present time he is wholly incapacitated for work,
having been absent from the office since the latter part of March, 1914.
